category_title: Preschoolers who cry when encountering perceived difficult tasks
minimal_context: Zeke is working on a fine motor bead-stringing activity at the Art center.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Zeke, here are the small beads and string for your art project.

STUDENT: (Whines softly) I can't put the string in.

TUTOR: Keep trying to push it through.

STUDENT: (Whines louder) It's too hard!

TUTOR: Just give it another try.

STUDENT: (Cries loudly and walks away from the table)

options.A: Reallocating paraprofessionals to paperwork tasks, thus freeing teachers to deliver instruction during fine motor activities at the Art center.
options.B: Prompting, modeling, role-playing, and explicitly teaching desired social-emotional behaviors (e.g., calming down when frustrated during fine motor tasks).
options.C: Providing individual storage space for materials at the Art center, such as chair bags or desks with compartments.
options.D: Increasing the time allotted for fine motor activities at the Art center from 15 minutes to 30 minutes.
